downgraded.text: The urns, pots and lachrymatories found in ancient graves are said still to recall these Ludki funerals.
downgraded.to_text: The urns, pots and lachrymatories found in ancient graves are said still to recall these Ludki.
downgraded.reason: The page says the grave urns "still remind us of these Ludki"; it does not say "funerals", so that added word is cut.

flagged.reason: Machal p.247 treats the Ludki as dwarfs, a race of small beings, which supports `other`; but the passage sits in the chapter "The Household Gods", ties dwarf myths to the worship of family genii, and says the Ludki lived partly in human dwellings, so `household` is a possible reading.

grade_rationale.text: Every surviving clause rests on one source, Machal's Slavic Mythology pp.247-248; a corpus search for Ludki and Ludek finds no other page.
Machal records the Ludki for one people only, the Lusatian Serbs (Sorbs).
Machal gives the belief as a summary in his own voice and names no collector or collected text for it, so the entry traces to a single compiler.
